div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center; width: 460px;

span.p:
Plus four service identities — sa-portal, sa-dashboard, sa-approvals, sa-binder.
sa-approvals is the only holder of the private signing key. The gateway holds
the public half and is structurally incapable of minting a token.

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center; width: 460px;

span.p:
Why the rows name collections, not services
a row that says Firestore cannot express the difference between the
qa_responses the Questionnaire agent must write and the findings it must never touch.
Vague permission rows are how least-privilege claims quietly become false.

div.style: color: rgb(120, 53, 15) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center;

span.p:
tests/test_iam_boundaries.py — 230 rows
every identity against every collection, evaluated by the emulator
against rules GENERATED from this matrix, so the two cannot drift.
44 permitted writes and 186 real PermissionDenied errors.
What it cannot prove — that sa-evidence is genuinely the principal.
That is a revision bound to a service account, and those rows stay
skipped with that as their stated reason.

div.style: color: rgb(15, 23, 42) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 460px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Why it is load-bearing
a fleet holding one god-credential is a single injection away
from disaster. Least privilege is what makes the screening story
true end to end — the agent that reads evidence cannot email,
and the agent that emails cannot touch internal data.

svg.text: Drawbridge — Zero-trust fleet identity: the permission matrix is a deliverable, not config
